description: Secondary storage is a non-volatile memory of a computer used to store data and information permanently. It primarily includes Hard Disk Drives (HDD), Solid State Drives (SSD), Optical Disks, and Magnetic Tapes.

sections.title: Hard Disk Drive (HDD)
sections.description: The primary and traditional magnetic storage device of a computer, used for storing massive amounts of data.

key_concepts.explanation: A data storage device that uses magnetic storage to store and retrieve digital information using one or more rigid rapidly rotating platters coated with magnetic material.
The surface of a hard disk is divided into concentric circles called tracks. Each track is further divided into smaller segments called sectors.
The time required for the read/write head of the hard disk to reach the desired track where the data is stored.
The rotational delay or the wait time required for the desired sector to rotate and come directly under the read/write head.

important_facts.fact: The standard storage capacity of a single sector on a hard disk is typically 512 bytes.

sections.title: Solid State Drive (SSD)
sections.description: A modern, highly efficient, and extremely fast data storage device that contains no moving mechanical parts.

key_concepts.explanation: A storage device that uses integrated circuit assemblies to store data persistently. Because it lacks moving parts, it is significantly faster, quieter, and more reliable than an HDD.
The type of non-volatile memory technology used in modern SSDs to store data, ensuring that the stored information remains intact even when the power is turned off.

important_facts.fact: Because SSDs have no physical read/write head or spinning platters, they have zero rotational delay and seek time, resulting in exceptionally high data transfer rates.

sections.title: Optical Disks
sections.description: Storage media that utilize optical technology, specifically laser beams, to read and write digital data.

key_concepts.explanation: A flat, usually circular disc where data is recorded by making marks in a pattern that can be read back with the aid of light, typically a laser beam. Data is stored in the form of 'Pits' and 'Lands'.

key_associations.extra_info: Primarily used in the past for storing audio files and small software packages.
Similar in physical size to a CD but offers significantly higher storage capacity, making it suitable for standard definition videos and movies.
Utilizes a blue-violet laser to read and write data, allowing it to store high-definition video (HD) and large modern video games.

sections.title: Magnetic Tapes and Other Devices
sections.description: Traditional and portable storage devices utilized for data archiving, backups, and data transfer.

key_concepts.explanation: A sequential access medium used for data storage. This means data can only be accessed in the exact order it was written. It is highly cost-effective and primarily used for large-scale data backups and archiving.
An obsolete magnetic storage medium consisting of a thin, flexible magnetic storage disk sealed in a rectangular plastic enclosure. Also known as a diskette.

key_associations.extra_info: The most common 3.5-inch floppy disk used extensively in the 1990s for transferring small text files and documents between computers.
A highly portable, plug-and-play flash memory storage device that connects to a computer via a USB port.

sections.title: Important Facts and Comparison
sections.description: Highly crucial one-liner facts and speed comparisons related to secondary storage from the perspective of competitive exams.

important_facts.fact: Secondary memory is also widely known as auxiliary memory, external memory, or mass storage.
Compared to primary memory (RAM), secondary memory operates at a much slower speed, but it provides a significantly larger storage capacity at a lower cost.
Order of Access Speed (Fastest to Slowest): Cache Memory > RAM > Solid State Drive (SSD) > Hard Disk Drive (HDD) > Optical Disk > Magnetic Tape.
Magnetic Tape is the only storage device that strictly supports 'Sequential Access' and does not support 'Direct Access' or 'Random Access'.
